redFirst.basis: tests.expectRedFirst is false on this tdd task: it names no case to prove a red by, so no red-first proof is owed

outcome.technical: Cause: lw1 handed dash sys.executable as a native Windows path made only of backslashes. A POSIX shell looks up a command name containing no slash on PATH, so dash printed 'not found'. Fix in tools/gate-parity.py: (1) new shell_spelled(path, sep=None), which returns the path unchanged when the separator is '/' and otherwise swaps the separator for '/'. That forward-slash form is what verify.sh gets from cygpath -m for a native program, and the same sys.executable.replace('\\','/') spelling the suites in tests/ already give Git Bash (test_stamp_verification's git filter, test_drive_phase's gate commands). It is the existing mechanism with a name, not a second one. (2) _run_live_window now sets LW_PY = shell_spelled(interpreter, sep) and takes optional cwd/executable/sep arguments, all defaulting to the old behaviour. (3) new _live_window_spelling_cases, called right after _live_window_cases. lw4: the Windows-shaped hostedtoolcache interpreter path with sep backslash becomes the forward-slash form, and a posix path is unchanged. lw5: on posix, the window step is run through _run_live_window with that Windows-shaped interpreter and a stand-in placed at the relative path C:/hostedtoolcache/.../python3.exe under a scratch cwd; it exits 0 and prints the step's argument. lw5w (the twin): the same interpreter passed through unspelled gives a non-zero exit and 'not found'. Under dash on this machine that is the CI line byte for byte: '/bin/dash: 1: C:\\hostedtoolcache\\...\\python3.exe: not found', code 127. On a platform whose own path module reads 'C:' as a drive (os.path.splitdrive), lw5 is _harness.skip'ped because the fixture directory cannot exist there, and lw1 runs the real interpreter through the same spelling instead; simulating ntpath.splitdrive on posix gives 'lw5 SKIPPED HERE', which passes. The 'no POSIX shell' path stays red as it was, never a skip, and no exception is read as a platform refusal. Results: gate-parity --selftest ALL PASS 127/127, exit 0 (was 56/57 before the fix); brief gate exit 0, '4/4 files ok'; verify.sh --affected exit 0, all 47 selected checks ok, including gate-parity.py, gate-parity.py --selftest and prove-gates.py --selftest; ruff check exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- exit 0. Only tools/gate-parity.py changed (91 insertions, 8 deletions). For the owner, on Windows, from the repo root in Git Bash: python tools/gate-parity.py --selftest | grep -E '^(PASS|FAIL) lw|cases passed' ; echo $? -- expected: 'PASS lw1 the shipped window step, run under dash.EXE ... code=0 ...' (shell name as which() finds it), PASS lw0, lw2, lw3, 'PASS lw4 ... C:/hostedtoolcache/windows/Python/3.12.10/x64/python3.exe ...', 'PASS lw5 SKIPPED HERE - this platform's path module reads `C:` as a drive ...', no lw5w line, then 'ALL PASS: N/N cases passed' and exit 0 (in PowerShell: python tools/gate-parity.py --selftest | Select-String '^(PASS|FAIL) lw|cases passed'). Dependants: tools/verify.sh names _live_window_cases, which keeps its name and contract, so it is still correct. ci.yml, sweep-costs.json, _areas.py, test_audit_task.py, affected.py, bench-hooks.py, _output_lints.py and measure-affected-miss.py read gate-parity by path or by names this change did not touch (floating_runners, image_in_job_names, job_bound_evidence and the like), so all are still correct. No repo file references shell_spelled, _run_live_window or the new cases (grep over .py/.sh/.md/.json). The other declared files (verify.sh, prove-gates.py, _harness.py, test__affected_tests.py, sweep-selftests.py, stamp-verification.py, test__runner_collects.py, test_stamp_verification.py, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md) were not edited, so their dependants are unchanged; the guide names no lw case or window-step interpreter. sweep-costs.json has no new block to weigh: the cases run inside gate-parity's existing body. Left as they are, outside this task's files: tests/test_py_launch.py:289 writes the raw sys.executable single-quoted into a /bin/sh shim, and test_drive_phase.py:826 and test_run_agent_session.py:157 do the same on their posix-only branches. None of them is in this CI failure.
outcome.descriptive: gate-parity lw1 now hands dash the interpreter in forward-slash form, so the window step should run on Windows (owner to confirm there); a posix case proves the conversion and its twin reproduces the CI failure
